ledger.note: 1346: the English take the Isle of Man for the last time. 'control passed back and forth between the two kingdoms until the English took it for the last time in 1346.' The Crown 'delegated its rule of the island to a series of lords and magnates'; the page names none of them for these years. Counterpart changed from kingdom-of-scotland by reviewer eu-11-j: the page has the English take the island in 1346, and the kingdom-of-scotland dossier already loses it to England in 1333 (contested to 1346).

1399: the Isle of Man comes under the feudal lordship of the English Crown. The page lead: 'the island came under the feudal lordship of the English Crown in 1399'; 'Since 1399, the kings and lords of Mann were vassals of the kings of England' (Lord of Mann page: 'Before 1504, the ruler of the Isle of Man was generally styled king of Mann'). Year is the page's; whether the Crown or Henry Percy took it directly is not on the pages.

wars.name: Struggle for the Isle of Man
wars.outcome: The island changed hands in 1313 (Scots, under Bruce), 1314 (English), 1317 (Scots, under Randolph), 1333 (Scots hold ends), and passed to the English 'for the last time in 1346'.
wars.note: Page: 'In 1290, King Edward I of England sent Walter de Huntercombe to take possession of Man... It remained in English hands until 1313, when Robert the Bruce of Scotland took it... In 1314, it was retaken for the English by John Bacach of Argyll... In 1317, it was retaken for the Scots by Thomas Randolph... held by the Scots until 1333'. The Isle of Man is the object of the war, not a belligerent.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is its border. Who ruled it under the Crown is not on the pages.

notes:
Written by eu-11-j on 2026-10-25 from two pages (budget 1-2).

Cliopatria's Isle of Man row is 1344-1401 and its seed has Scotland as its only neighbour. The pages give: Scots until 1333; back and forth until the English took it 'for the last time in 1346'; 'under the feudal lordship of the English Crown in 1399'. The dossier therefore runs 1346-1399 (found and dissolve at confidence 3 and 2); the two keyframes are 'adjust' (years only, shape unchanged). The gap 1400-1401 is covered by neither this row nor Cliopatria's Kingdom of England (which includes the island from 1402); the England dossier (eu-11, another part) should start the island at 1399.
The 14th-century lords (the Lord of Mann page has none before its list of 1504), the date of any forfeiture, and the Percy and Stanley lordships beyond the 1405 and 1406 letters patent that the page calls void are not on the pages opened and are not recorded. A gap-filler could open 'History of the Isle of Man' for the 14th-century lordship and the date Cliopatria uses for 1344.
The Isle of Man is the same entity as the modern Crown dependency (Q9676), and the Lord of Mann page runs the lordship to 1765 (purchase by the British government) and 1828; Cliopatria's later rows carry the island inside England and Great Britain, so this dossier stops in 1399 (a later Crown-dependency dossier could be added by the colonial-empire group).
The Scottish gains and losses of the island (1313, 1314, 1317, 1333, contest 1333-1346) are in the kingdom-of-scotland dossier; the matching losses are expected in the kingdom-of-england dossier.
Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-england (the Crown), kingdom-of-scotland (mine). Gazetteer: no new names (Isle of Man exists as country, admin1 and region).
